m.t: Tagging pillars at the Brimhaven Agility Arena
m.pg: Money making guide/Exchanging agility arena tickets for pirate hook

rq.h: High healing food (Shark or higher)
Spotted or Spottier cape, or Wicked cape
200 coins for entry (optional)

m.h:
The profit rate assumes 65 tickets per hour.

Refer to Brimhaven Agility Arena on methods to get there and the different types of methods you will face.

A Pirate hook costs 800 tickets, this is the only method that can obtain this item. Each ticket would be worth 125,678.12 gp each.

Without Karamja gloves 4, it takes a minimum of 800 minutes (or 13 hours 20 minutes) to earn enough tickets - worth an average of 7,540,688 gp per hour (assuming no pillars are missed). The minimum time required to earn these tickets is reduced to 640 minutes (or 10 hours 40 minutes) when wearing Karamja gloves 4 because of the bonus tickets received - worth an average of 9,425,859 gp per hour (assuming no pillars are missed).

Note that the pirate hook has a very low trade volume and may take a while to sell.

m.post:
Farming arbuck can be a very profitable way to spend a few minutes at a time. To maximise profit, use the following items to maximise the crop yield:

  • Magic secateurs from A Fairy Tale I - Growing Pains, which boosts crop yield by 10%.
  • Juju farming potion from Herblore Habitat, which gives a 33% chance of picking double herbs, effectively increasing crop yield by 33%.
  • Master farmer outfit, which boosts crop yield by 10% and automatically clean the herbs gathered.
  • Scroll of life, which gives a 10% chance of returning your seed after you've harvested the crop.
  • Unlocking Plant Power Tier 4 from the Garden of Kharid allows you to plant 10 seeds at once, increasing overall output.
  • Unlocking Bountiful Harvest 2 from the Garden of Kharid gives a 7% chance of an additional item upon each harvest.

Without these items, herb farming is much less profitable.

Items such as the Farmer's outfit and Falador shield 2 or higher will also increase experience gained. A modified farmer's hat will also save sowed seeds 2% of the time and offers 3 free teleports to the Morytania allotment per day.

Start your run with 8-80 arbuck seeds, 8 ultracompost, transportation to get to all eight patches, and whatever yield- and experience-boosting items you have. At each location, harvest any available herbs, note them with the tool leprechaun, compost the patch, and plant new seeds.

Order of steps
  • The Wilderness Patch is located in level 38 Wilderness; ensure you are opted out of PvP, else you will not be able to use conventional teleports to escape. If opted into PvP, you can use the Wilderness obelisk nearby to reach lower level Wilderness. Alternatively, run south to level 30 Wilderness and escape via an amulet of glory, a Ring of Wealth, a combat bracelet, or a Saradominist/Zamorakian token.

From start to finish, this process takes about seven minutes, and the new seeds you planted can be checked in 80 minutes. You could sell your herbs immediately after each run, or wait to sell them. You may also want to consider cleaning the herbs for additional profit, if you do not have the Master farmer outfit, which does this automatically.

rq.q: A Fairy Tale I - Growing Pains

m.h:
Farming godly grapes and turning them into wine can be very profitable as the wines (mainly Wine of Zamorak and Wine of Saradomin) are used for popular high-level potions. To maximise profit, you should have:

  • Magic secateurs from A Fairy Tale I - Growing Pains, which boost yield 10%

Without these items, godly grape farming is much less profitable. Normal, oak, teak, or mahogany planks may be used to build the vine frame; this guide uses s, as they are currently the cheapest.

Begin your run at Seers' Village with 10 s, 8 godly grapevine seeds, and 2 supercompost. Pick the grapes from the patch, using the leprechaun to note all grapes. When the patch is empty, apply supercompost first, then build a frame with 5 planks, and finally plant the seeds.

Use Watchtower Teleport next, exit the building and go directly east and use the underwall tunnel agility shortcut to cross into Yanille. Repeat the process for harvesting and planting grapes here. Run to the bank and take out 10 more planks, 8 more seeds, and 2 more supercompost.

The next patch should be the Lumbridge patch. Travel here by using the combat bracelet teleport to the Champion's Guild and running south-east, jump over the fence. Harvest the grapevines.

Next you should teleport to Port Sarim (a captain's log is the best option) and take the boat to Entrana. The patch is directly west of where the boat will take you. In case you have any equipment that is not allowed on the boat (like the Farming cape) use the deposit box by the boat. Once there harvest and plant your grapes.

Finally, teleport to any bank and create wine. Grapes can be used on the jugs of water or vice versa. Also, note that wine can ferment in the bank, so you do not need to wait for it to ferment before starting a new inventory.

m.h:
As a tertiary ingredient used in the Summoning skill, marigolds are always in demand. And with Farming being almost the only source of marigolds, the demand is not always met. Farming marigolds can thus be somewhat profitable for low-level players, as it requires only level 2 Farming and is even available to non-members.

Members have access to four farming patches in which marigolds can be farmed - one near Falador, one near Port Phasmatys, one in Catherby and one at the Manor Farm. Only the one near Falador is available to free players, so if you're not a member you'll make roughly one quarter of the profits listed here. Apart from membership, none of these patches have any requirements to access, but the one by Port Phasmatys can be time-consuming to get to without the ectophial or a modified farmer's hat (the latter of which can only be used three times a day) - the easiest way to get there without either of those is teleporting to the Canifis lodestone, though skipping the patch might be a better option. The Falador patch also takes a little bit of time to reach without the Explorer's ring 3 or the South Falador Teleport spell, although the Draynor Village lodestone is reasonably close by. The Manor Farm and Catherby patches are easy to reach with the lodestone Network, and should always be used.

Every five minutes while growing, marigolds have a risk of becoming diseased. When diseased, the marigolds have a roughly 50% risk of dying every 5 minutes and will not grow further unless cured using plant cure. As the frequency of disease isn't known, the profit calculation doesn't include this - actual profit may be somewhat lower than the listed number for this reason. Using compost, supercompost, or ultracompost reduces the risk of this happening, although the cost of the compost may outweight the benefits this involves - this is certainly the case for the rather expensive ultracompost, but might not be for the cheaper compost or supercompost.

To help you keep track of when your marigolds have finished growing, you may want to use an out-of-game timer and/or wear an amulet of farming.

When you expect the marigolds to be fully grown (roughly 20 minutes after planting), head to each of the patches you used and pick the marigolds. If they died, clear the patch instead. If they are alive but diseased, the nearby farmers sell plant cure for 25 coins if you talk to them - you won't get any marigolds this time around, but it saves you a seed. Once you have picked the flowers or cleared the patch, plant another marigold seed. You may want to add compost or supercompost before planting the seed. Then head to the next patch if there are any left, or a bank or the Grand Exchange when you're finished with all the patches.

Buying marigold seeds from the Draynor Seed Market might be cheaper than buying them off the Grand Exchange. The seeds are cheap enough compared to the flowers that this should not make a large difference, however.

m.h:
There are three mushroom patches. Start at the mushroom patch west of Canifis. The simplest way to get to the patch is by using the fairy ring , which teleports you steps from the patch. Once you're there, harvest the mushrooms and plant new ones. Next teleport to the Isafdar patch directly with the Tirannwn quiver 3 or use the Tirannwn lodestone and go west through the dense forest then run south to the Isafdar mushroom patch. Harvest and replant the mushrooms. Finally, if you have 80 Necromancy, teleport to the City of Um using the Underworld Grimoire (Um smithy) and go west to the mushroom patch. Harvest, and replant the mushrooms there. Alternatively, if the Passing bracelet is obtained, players can rub the bracelet and choose the first option (City of Um: Hanging Gardens) The patches have a growing time of 240 minutes - reduced to 200 if the spores are planted with a Sunburst bracelet equipped.

The Morytania achievements help immensely for growing morchella mushrooms -- after completing the Medium achievements, the Morytania patch will be immune from disease, so no supercompost is necessary. However, it is advised to use supercompost on the Isafdar patch as this may become diseased. Also, the Pharm Ecology relic power protects the mushroom patches, laying off the need for supercompost. After completing the Elite Morytania achievements, you'll get double the mushrooms that you would normally, 18 instead of 9, from all patches per patch. The profit above is calculated with the Morytania Elite and Tirannwn Medium achievements completed, but this method is worth doing even if you haven't completed them.

m.post:
Farming ranarr can be a very profitable way to spend a few minutes at a time. To maximise profit, use the following items to maximise the crop yield:

  • Magic secateurs from A Fairy Tale I - Growing Pains, which boosts crop yield by 10%.
  • Juju farming potion from Herblore Habitat, which gives a 33% chance of picking double herbs, effectively increasing crop yield by 33%.
  • Master farmer outfit, which boosts crop yield by 10% and automatically clean the herbs gathered.
  • Scroll of life, which gives a 10% chance of returning your seed after you've harvested the crop.
  • Unlocking Plant Power Tier 4 from the Garden of Kharid allows you to plant 10 seeds at once, increasing overall output.
  • Unlocking Bountiful Harvest 2 from the Garden of Kharid gives a 7% chance of an additional item upon each harvest.

Without these items, herb farming is much less profitable.

Items such as the Farmer's outfit and Falador shield 2 or higher will also increase experience gained. A modified farmer's hat will also save sowed seeds 2% of the time and offers 3 free teleports to the Morytania allotment per day.

Start your run with 8-80 ranarr seeds, 8 ultracompost, transportation to get to all eight patches, and whatever yield- and experience-boosting items you have. At each location, harvest any available herbs, note them with the tool leprechaun, compost the patch, and plant new seeds.

Order of steps
  • The Wilderness Patch is located in level 38 Wilderness; ensure you are opted out of PvP, else you will not be able to use conventional teleports to escape. If opted into PvP, you can use the Wilderness obelisk nearby to reach lower level Wilderness. Alternatively, run south to level 30 Wilderness and escape via an amulet of glory, a Ring of Wealth, a combat bracelet, or a Saradominist/Zamorakian token.

From start to finish, this process takes about seven minutes, and the new seeds you planted can be checked in 80 minutes. You could sell your herbs immediately after each run, or wait to sell them. You may also want to consider cleaning the herbs for additional profit, if you do not have the Master farmer outfit, which does this automatically.

out.nt: Accounts for the 25% boost to Starbloom flowers from the Zolarea flower patch - harvesting 15 flowers instead of 12 (without Dwarven harvester).

m.post:
Due to their high demand in crafting Starbloom and Masterwork magic equipment, farming Starbloom flowers can be a profitable way to spend a few minutes.

  • Sunburst bracelet will skip a growth phase entirely, allowing the flowers to be harvested sooner, assuming they do not get diseased.
    • Alternatively, Master farming outfit can automatically water flower patches, significantly reducing their chance to become diseased. However, plants will require an extra growth cycle over using the bracelet.
  • Scroll of Life has no effect on flower patches, but Modified farmer's hat will still have a chance to save the seed and battlestaff when planting.
  • Dwarven harvester can be used to double the yield from harvesting the flowers, giving no harvest experience in the process.
  • Applying Supercompost or using the Farming master cape's passive effect can be used to mitigate the odds of the flowers becoming diseased.
Order of steps
